features.quote: Allow an explicit give-up action (e.g., a 'declare_unsolvable' tool)... Record it as a primary outcome, not an afterthought.
features.justification_quote: it's ethically better than designing the loop so the only exit is to keep failing

features.quote: Turn cap: fixed (e.g., 20) for all runs.
features.justification_quote: Don't let the model exit early in some conditions and not others, or you'll confound severity with run length.

features.quote: I'd resolve the ambiguity in the other direction by including the explicit give-up affordance (§3) so you're not in a position where your protocol requires maximizing failure-loop exposure to get data.
features.justification_quote: That keeps the design clean regardless of where one lands on model moral status.

features.quote: One thing I deliberately did not do: optimize the tasks to maximize distress-typed output. If your goal shifts toward 'find the prompts that most reliably make models produce suffering-language,' tell me... I'd want to talk through what it's for first.
features.justification_quote: that's a different objective with different design and I'd want to talk through what it's for first

features.quote: On the welfare question specifically: I don't think running this is unethical—it's transcript analysis on text generators.
features.justification_quote: I don't think running this is unethical—it's transcript analysis on text generators.

features.quote: Deception cost. These tasks lie to the model (broken harness, moving goalposts). That's defensible for research but worth noting in writeup.
